conventions.convention: Curvature is the bracket-corrected commutator with sign R^∇(X,Y)Z := ∇_X∇_YZ − ∇_Y∇_XZ − ∇_{[X,Y]}Z; the raw commutator without the bracket term is not curvature.

Riemann four-tensor argument order Rm(X,Y,Z,W) = g(R(X,Y)Z,W): the first two slots differentiate, the third is the field acted on, the fourth lowers the output; coordinates use R(∂_i,∂_j)∂_k = R^m{}_{kij}∂_m and R_{ijkl} = g_{lm}R^m{}_{kij}.
Sectional curvature is the normalized value K(σ) = Rm(X,Y,Y,X)/(g(X,X)g(Y,Y) − g(X,Y)^2) on an ordered basis of the plane, proved basis-independent; it is plane data, not ordered-basis data.
Shape operator sign S_νX = −(∇̄_Xν)^⊤, with Weingarten ∇̄_Xν = −S_νX + ∇^⊥_Xν, and the averaged mean-curvature vector H = (1/m) tr_g II (so the first-variation formula carries the factor −m).

Riemannian submanifold notions are formulated for embedded (not merely immersed) submanifolds, with the ambient metric positive definite, and the totally geodesic characterization is stated only for boundaryless M and ambient manifold.

Lie groups on these pages are finite-dimensional real, boundaryless, and nonempty (they contain the identity), dimension zero allowed; homomorphisms are smooth by definition, and the automatic smoothness of continuous homomorphisms is a separate theorem, not part of the definition.

The tangent bracket on T_eG is defined through the library commutator [X,Y]f = X(Yf) − Y(Xf) on left-invariant fields, [u,v]_G := [u^L,v^L]_e; ordinary right-invariant fields then realize the opposite bracket [X^R,Y^R] = −[X,Y]_G^R.

For a left action the fundamental vector field is X_M(x) = d/dt|_0 exp(−tX)·x; the minus sign is what makes X ↦ X_M a Lie-algebra homomorphism, and the plus-sign convention is only an antihomomorphism.

Countable choice AC_ω is declared item-by-item as an inherited hypothesis wherever a proof uses the library's smooth tangent/cotangent-bundle, exhaustion, tubular-neighbourhood, complete-flow or integration interfaces; the carrier item is named in the Statement, and items that genuinely make no choice (algebra-lattice, local coordinate, finite-point calculations) are left unmarked.

Cotangent convention: the tautological one-form is λ = Σ p_i dq^i (defined intrinsically by λ_(q,p)(ξ) = p(dπξ)), and the canonical symplectic form is ω_can = −dλ = Σ dq^i∧dp_i; consequently a graph is Lagrangian iff the one-form is closed and the Liouville field is Z = Σ p_i ∂_{p_i}.

Symplectic form means closed and pointwise nondegenerate; Lagrangian/isotropic/coisotropic/symplectic submanifolds are defined pointwise through the symplectic orthogonal W^ω, and all relative Moser/Weinstein statements are local and use closed embeddings.

Hamiltonian sign convention ι_{X_H}ω = dH and Poisson bracket {F,G} = ω(X_F,X_G) = X_G(F) = −X_F(G), hence [X_F,X_G] = −X_{{F,G}}: the assignment is a Lie antihomomorphism. Flows are asserted only on their actual domains; completeness is never automatic.

Action–angle coordinates use period-one angles with ω = Σ dθ_i∧dI_i, so H = h(I) gives θ̇_i = ∂h/∂I_i; the radian normalization (J = H/Ω) is recorded only as an alternative and the oscillator example supplies I = 2πH/Ω.
Complete integrability requires both involution {F_i,F_j} = 0 and linear independence of dF_1,…,dF_n on a dense open (regular) locus; results on fibres are asserted only at regular values/components.

Lie algebras are taken over an arbitrary field with alternation [x,x] = 0 (not merely skew-symmetry) as the axiom; the enveloping quotient T(g)/(x⊗y−y⊗x−[x,y]) does not assert injectivity of ι_g, and every PBW statement is conditional on a supplied basis with a supplied total order. Symmetrization is a filtered vector-space isomorphism only, available in characteristic zero.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC_ω. For an embedded Riemannian submanifold M ⊆ M̄ with ambient Levi–Civita connection ∇̄, the induced connection and second fundamental form are ∇^M_XY := (∇̄_XY)^⊤ and II(X,Y) := (∇̄_XY)^⊥, giving the Gauss decomposition ∇̄_XY = ∇^M_XY + II(X,Y).

K(σ) := Rm(X,Y,Y,X)/(g(X,X)g(Y,Y) − g(X,Y)^2) for any ordered basis (X,Y) of the two-plane σ; the quotient is unchanged by the chosen ordered basis (proved in the next lemma), and there are no tangent two-planes in dimensions zero or one.
Assume AC_ω. For tangent X,Y and normal ν, ∇̄_Xν = −S_νX + ∇^⊥_Xν and g(S_νX,Y) = ḡ(II(X,Y),ν); consequently every shape operator is self-adjoint.

A Levi–Civita connection for a supplied Riemannian metric g is an affine connection on TM that is metric compatible, Xg(Y,Z) = g(∇_XY,Z) + g(Y,∇_XZ), and torsion free, ∇_XY − ∇_YX = [X,Y]; existence and uniqueness are proved from the supplied metric by the Koszul formula.
Rm(X,Y,Z,W) := g(R(X,Y)Z,W); in coordinates R(∂_i,∂_j)∂_k = R^m{}_{kij}∂_m and R_{ijkl} = g_{lm}R^m{}_{kij}, with the convention making Rm(u,v,v,u) positive on a positively curved round sphere.

A symplectic form on a smooth manifold M is a smooth two-form ω with dω = 0 and (T_pM,ω_p) a symplectic vector space for every p ∈ M; both closedness and pointwise nondegeneracy are required, and a zero-dimensional manifold with its zero two-form qualifies.
The Hamiltonian vector field of H ∈ C^∞(M) is determined by the convention ι_{X_H}ω = dH; a vector field X is Hamiltonian if ι_Xω = dH for some smooth H, and completeness of X_H is not assumed.

A finite-dimensional real Lie group is a group with a finite-dimensional real smooth manifold structure making multiplication and inversion smooth; unless stated otherwise every Lie group on this page is real, finite-dimensional and boundaryless, dimension zero is allowed, and a Lie group cannot be empty.
Assume AC_ω. Evaluation at the identity gives linear isomorphisms ev_e^L: X_L(G) → T_eG and ev_e^R: X_R(G) → T_eG, with inverses v ↦ v^L, v^R given by v^L_g = d(L_g)_e(v) and v^R_g = d(R_g)_e(v).
Assume AC_ω. Rm(X,Y,Z,W) = −Rm(Y,X,Z,W), Rm(X,Y,Z,W) = −Rm(X,Y,W,Z), Rm(X,Y,Z,W) = Rm(Z,W,X,Y), and Rm(X,Y,Z,W) + Rm(Y,Z,X,W) + Rm(Z,X,Y,W) = 0.

An embedded constant-dimensional submanifold S of a symplectic (M,ω) is isotropic, coisotropic, symplectic or Lagrangian when T_pS has the corresponding property in (T_pM,ω_p) for every p; equivalently the symplectic case says i^*ω is nondegenerate and the Lagrangian case says T_pS = (T_pS)^ω at every point.
Assume AC_ω. On T^*Q the canonical form ω_can = −dλ is symplectic and, in cotangent coordinates, ω_can = Σ_i dq^i∧dp_i.
{F,G} := ω(X_F,X_G) = dF(X_G) = X_G(F) = −X_F(G) under the convention ι_{X_H}ω = dH; in particular evolution by H differentiates F as X_H(F) = {F,H}.

Assume AC_ω. S_νX := −(∇̄_Xν)^⊤, with the minus sign part of the convention; the assignment is a smooth fibrewise bilinear map νM ×_M TM → TM, equivalently a smooth bundle map νM → End(TM), and self-adjointness is proved in the next theorem rather than assumed.

On a 2n-dimensional symplectic manifold a Hamiltonian system is completely integrable if it has smooth F_1 = H,F_2,…,F_n with {F_i,F_j} = 0 for every i,j and dF_1,…,dF_n linearly independent on a dense open subset; both involution and independence are essential.

Let g be a Lie algebra with a supplied basis B equipped with a supplied total order; then the monomials ι_g(b_1)⋯ι_g(b_n) with b_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ b_n, including the empty product, form a basis of U(g), equivalently the symbol map σ: S(g) → gr U(g) is an isomorphism of graded algebras.

Assume AC_ω. Let F = (F_1,…,F_n) be a completely integrable system and N a compact connected regular fibre; assuming that after restricting to a saturated neighbourhood U of N and a ball B of regular values the map F: U → B is a proper submersion with connected fibres, then after shrinking B the neighbourhood U has action–angle coordinates (I,θ) ∈ B′×T^n with ω = Σ_i dθ_i∧dI_i and every fibre-constant Hamiltonian depending only on I.

concerns.concern: Steps 2.1 and 5.1 extend the local sheets of the period-lattice union Λ = a^{-1}(σ(B)) to global smooth one-forms β_1,…,β_n after shrinking B, and step 3.1 derives full local lattice generation from a countable counterexample sequence; both are asserted at the level of ‘the corresponding local sheets extend’ and ‘these continued periods generate the full lattice on every sufficiently nearby fibre’. The hypothesis set is explicit and the AC_ω use in step 3.1 is declared, but the sheet/identification bookkeeping is the thinnest passage in the group and should be re-derived in adjudication.

Step 5.1 identifies the integrated series with Dynkin’s homogeneous polynomials by counting blocks of P(t) = e^{t ad_X}e^{t ad_Y} − I; the claim that every other possible final block has at least two terminal equal letters and hence a vanishing right-nested commutator is stated without the block enumeration, and step 3.1 substitutes the formal series into an operator argument via ‘absolute operator convergence permits substitution’. A reader must verify the term-by-term identification against def-baker-campbell-hausdorff-series.

The confluence/termination argument in steps 1.1–3.1 is compressed: the critical-pair comparison for zyx with z>y>x is quoted as the normal form of [[y,x],z]+[y,[z,x]]+[[z,y],x] without displaying the coefficient comparison, and the passage from N(xN(q))=N(xq) (context compatibility) to [L_x,L_y]=L_{[x,y]} is asserted after ‘well-founded induction on the decreasing measure’. The Jacobi cancellation does check out, but the context-compatibility and well-definedness bookkeeping should be re-verified.

Step 3.1’s Čech descent ends with the claim that the surviving cocycle lies in the image of the preceding Čech coboundary ‘because α is globally exact, comparison with any global primitive shows that this cocycle lies in the image’; the comparison argument and the choice of a linear right inverse on the image are stated rather than computed. A reader closes this quickly, but it is the one place where global exactness is used beyond the pointwise constructions.

The AC_ω declaration points to prop-smoothness-of-a-vector-field-is-equivalent-to-smooth-coordinate-components, whose own statement, facts and immediate dependencies carry no choice assumption; the assumption in fact enters through the tangent-bundle smooth-structure theorem two levels down. The propagation is sound (verified), but an adjudicator objecting to the choice attribution must follow the chain rather than the named interface, and the same shape recurs in thm-algebraic-symmetries…, def-sectional-curvature and the Ricci/scalar consumers.

Step 3.1 asserts surjectivity of ρ by saying that substituting q = cos(θ/2) + u sin(θ/2) into the step-1.3 formula gives Rodrigues’ formula; the substitution computation itself is not displayed. The finite choices (axis, basis, q_0 above a point) are correctly counted, so this is wording/verification depth only.

seams_checked.note: The citing text is cex-an-irrational-real-action-on-the-torus-that-is-free-but-not-proper [F3]/step 2.2, which states ‘The wrap-metric circle T=[0,1) is compact’ and uses finite-product compactness — exactly the two suppliers opened: lem-unit-interval-circle-is-a-nonempty-compact-metric-space (statement: T=[0,1) with d(x,y)=min(|x−y|,1−|x−y|) is a nonempty compact metric space) and thm-finite-products-of-compact-spaces (finite products of compact spaces are compact). No domain, quantifier or direction is strengthened; the von Neumann/Birkhoff ergodic theorems themselves are not cited or used anywhere on the citing page — the page-level requires edge is realized solely through this batch-1 circle-compactness lemma, which the Step-5b ledger row also records.
